title: Burden of non-communicable diseases in Health Council of Gulf Cooperation (GCC) countries
key_finding: Nine NCDs caused about 153,000 deaths and US$23.9 bn in lost economic output across GCC countries; ischaemic heart disease alone accounted for over half of deaths and losses.

title: Measuring progress towards universal health coverage in 22 Middle East and North African countries
key_finding: The 2021 UHC index ran from 48 to 90 across MENA, with the UAE highest; service coverage trails financial protection in most countries and rises with income.

title: Projected impact of population aging on non-communicable disease burden and costs in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, 2020-2030
key_finding: Ageing pushes the cost of managing priority NCDs in Saudi Arabia from about US$19.8 bn (2020) to US$32.4 bn (2030), a 63% rise led by osteoarthritis, diabetes and dementia.

title: The Profile of Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) research in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region
key_finding: Maps NCD research output against disease burden in ten MENA countries; output is uneven across countries and is compared with each country's wealth and disease burden.

title: A Systematic Review of the Economic Burden of Diabetes in Eastern Mediterranean Region Countries
key_finding: Summarises cost-of-illness studies of diabetes published 2010–2023 in the region, breaking costs into direct medical, non-medical and indirect components.

title: The economic burden of overweight and obesity in Saudi Arabia
key_finding: Overweight and obesity cost about US$3.8 bn in direct medical spending (4.3% of health spending) in 2019, plus about US$15.5 bn in lost productivity (0.9% of GDP).

title: The Epidemiology and Economic Burden of Obesity and Related Cardiometabolic Disorders in the United Arab Emirates
key_finding: All 36 studies found high obesity, diabetes and hypertension; only one costed diabetes, at about US$2,015 per patient a year, rising sharply with complications.

journal: Int J Environ Res Public Health
title: Households' Direct Economic Burden Associated with Chronic Non-Communicable Diseases in Saudi Arabia
key_finding: About 40% of Riyadh households surveyed had a member with a chronic NCD; the study measures their out-of-pocket spending by condition

title: Utilization and cost of drugs for diabetes and its comorbidities and complications in Kuwait
key_finding: Of 1,182 patients, 41% had complications; 86% used oral antidiabetics and half used insulin, giving a basis for drug-budget forecasting.

title: Arab Countries and Oncology Clinical Trials: A Bibliometric Analysis
key_finding: Arab centres took part in 320 published cancer drug trials (2000–2021); numbers are rising, but most trials were small and lacked external funding.

title: Barriers and Facilitators to Conducting Oncology Clinical Trials in the UAE
key_finding: Sets out institutional, regulatory, patient and industry barriers that hold back cancer trials in the UAE, and what would help.

title: Migration of nurses and doctors: pull factors to work in Saudi Arabia
key_finding: Pay and rewards, entry requirements, religion, family and work environment draw migrant doctors and nurses to Saudi Arabia.

title: Nurse Migration and Workforce Dynamics in the Eastern Mediterranean Region
key_finding: The region both sends and receives nurses; shortages, rising demand and instability are intensifying cross-border nurse migration.

title: Health workforce capacity of intensive care units in the Eastern Mediterranean Region
key_finding: Finds shortages of intensive-care staff and gaps in training, working conditions and appraisal across the region, with limited data.

title: Bed Surge Capacity in Saudi Hospitals During the COVID-19 Pandemic
key_finding: Estimates Saudi hospitals would need about 4,400 extra beds over a six-month surge, a template for bed-capacity planning.

title: Digital health in fragile states in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region: A scoping review of the literature
key_finding: 93 studies, mostly observational, on digital tools for providers, patients and data; very little on health-system or management uses.

title: The Usage of Digital Health Mobile-Based Applications among Saudi Population
key_finding: Most respondents could afford smartphones, had at least one health app and valued their benefits: a ready market for scaling digital health.

title: Guided digital health intervention for depression in Lebanon: randomised trial
key_finding: A guided digital programme (Step-by-Step) for 680 adults clearly reduced depression, anxiety and impaired functioning compared with usual care.

title: Prevalence of Obesity and Overweight among Adults in the Middle East Countries from 2000 to 2020
key_finding: Across 101 studies (about 700,000 adults), about 21% were obese and 33% overweight, with obesity rising with age.

title: Prevalence, risk factors, and interventions for obesity in Saudi Arabia: A systematic review
key_finding: Reviews 59 prevalence studies and 29 intervention studies (drug, lifestyle and surgery) on Saudi Arabia's above-average obesity rate.

title: An alarmingly high and increasing prevalence of obesity in Jordan
key_finding: By waist circumference, about 60% of men and 76% of women in Jordan had abdominal obesity; about three-quarters were overweight or obese.

title: Tobacco Smoking Prevalence, Health Risk, and Cessation in the UAE
key_finding: The first UAE review of smoking prevalence, risks and cessation (14 studies) found widely varying estimates and few cessation interventions.

title: Prevalence of Childhood Obesity Among Children and Adolescents in Saudi Arabia: A Systematic Review
key_finding: Traces the prevalence and trend of obesity among Saudi 2–19-year-olds over 24 years.

title: Noncommunicable diseases and health system responses in Saudi Arabia: focus on policies and strategies. A qualitative study
key_finding: Officials judged Ministry of Health NCD programmes an early success but not yet properly evaluated; tobacco, sugary-drink and obesity policies moved faster than other areas.

title: Evaluating the health system financing of the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) countries using Grey Relation Analysis and Shannon Entropy
key_finding: EMR countries spent on average 4.9% of GDP on health (2005–2014); Qatar ranked first on health financing, followed by the UAE and Kuwait, with wide inequality across the region.

title: The Effects of Health Insurance on Health-Seeking Behaviour: Evidence from the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
key_finding: Having health insurance raised the chance of regular check-ups, more so for non-Saudis and holders of personal policies, and nudged people with hypertension to seek care.

title: The cascade of care in managing hypertension in the Arab world: a systematic assessment of the evidence on awareness, treatment and control
key_finding: Across 73 studies, large shares of people with hypertension were lost at each care step: over 40% were unaware of their condition, a key gap for treatment and adherence programmes.

title: Glycaemic control for people with type 2 diabetes in Saudi Arabia - an urgent need for a review of management plan
key_finding: Among 1,111 adults with type 2 diabetes, mean HbA1c was 8.5% and about three in four were above the 7% target.

title: The prevalence and determinants of poor glycemic control among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus in Saudi Arabia
key_finding: 75% of patients had poor glycaemic control; family history, longer disease duration and low physical activity raised the odds.

title: Nursing workforce challenges in gulf cooperation council countries: A systematic review of factors influencing shortage and retention
key_finding: Poor work environments, weak leadership support and heavy workloads (reported by about 59% of nurses) drive turnover; over 60% reported emotional exhaustion.

title: Current status of telehealth in Saudi Arabia during COVID-19
key_finding: Reviews how Saudi Arabia scaled telehealth services and apps during COVID-19 and what remains to build them into routine care.
